hero.description: Assess order risk, follow up manually through WhatsApp or phone, and record confirmation outcomes in one merchant workflow.

identity.title: Resolve the Hidden Connections Between Orders
identity.subtitle: Single-order checks miss coordinated fraudsters. ORDIUM constructs a real-time entity resolution graph across devices, addresses, phone numbers, and payment tokens.
identity.network_ip_desc: Residential proxy check, Tor node registry, and ASN reputation.
identity.graph_hint: INTERACTIVE GRAPH: HOVER NODES TO INSPECT
identity.hardware_fp_desc: Canvas hash, WebGL hardware profile, and emulator detection.
identity.order_history_desc: Cart item velocity, repeat card trials, and baseline behavioral cadence.
identity.phone_carrier_desc: VOIP detection, prepaid line classification, and SIM-swap indicators.
identity.customer_identity_desc: Cross-merchant velocity and synthetic identity anomaly scoring.
identity.address_clustering_desc: Drop address detection, commercial freight forwarders, and geo-variance.

pipeline.title: Deterministic 5-Stage Decision Engine
pipeline.subtitle: From store cart checkout to post-settlement feedback loop, every transaction traverses a transparent, low-latency evaluation path.
pipeline.stage_1_desc: Ingest customer profile, billing, shipping address, IP, and hardware canvas fingerprint.
pipeline.stage_2_desc: Map entities across cross-merchant graph clusters to uncover synthetic account rings.
pipeline.stage_3_desc: Execute merchant-configured velocity rules, Tor/VPN detection, and threshold policies.
pipeline.stage_4_desc: Calculate 0–100 risk score and emit immediate ALLOW, REVIEW, or REJECT decision.
pipeline.stage_5_desc: Ingest chargeback and legitimate fulfillment feedback to continuously refine heuristics.
pipeline.step_7_desc: Finalizes the decision: ALLOW, REVIEW or REJECT, using the store risk-profile thresholds (defaults: review at 50, reject at 80).
pipeline.step_3_desc: Examines checkout duration, velocity spikes, and interaction cadence.
pipeline.step_6_desc: Calculates unified 0-100 risk score with dimensional sub-scores.
pipeline.step_1_desc: Normalized checkout payload arrives via API, webhook, or SDK.
pipeline.step_5_desc: Weights verified signals against merchant policy rules & thresholds.
pipeline.step_4_desc: Inspects IP egress, VPN/Tor, ASN reputation, and geo-distance variance.
pipeline.step_2_desc: Resolves customer, phone, device, and email into graph entities.

explainable.title: Built for explainable decisions.
explainable.subtitle: Risk decisions expose the persisted signals, rule version, and evaluation metadata available to the merchant.
explainable.reject_rationale: Aggregated risk exceeds the merchant reject threshold of 75. Order blocked from payment authorization.
explainable.sig_net_desc: IP mapped directly to active Tor exit node registry.
explainable.sig_dev_desc: Hardware fingerprint dev_8f0a observed across 3 distinct cards in 2h.
explainable.sig_cluster_desc: Phone and shipping address linked to multi-actor cluster #CL-441.
explainable.sig_velo_desc: 14 rapid checkout attempts observed on subnet in past 60 minutes.
explainable.sig_cancel_desc: Connected drop address has an 80% past cancellation/chargeback rate.

fraud_cluster.title: Detect patterns before they become losses.
fraud_cluster.subtitle: A single suspicious order might pass a traditional basic check. But when ORDIUM joins phone numbers, device IDs, and IP subnets across multiple transactions, the fraudulent ring becomes instantly apparent.
fraud_cluster.step1_desc: Order #1 uses a clean synthetic email and passes standard postal address formatting checks. Single-point filters see no red flags.
fraud_cluster.step2_title: Entity Links Collide in ORDIUM Graph
fraud_cluster.step2_desc: Within 2 hours, Orders #2 and #3 arrive with different cardholder names but match the same hardware fingerprint and VoIP phone trunk.
fraud_cluster.step3_desc: ORDIUM automatically groups all 4 related identities into a high-risk syndicate cluster, elevating risk score to 82+ and neutralizing further attempts.
fraud_cluster.chargebacks_avoided: Outcome impact is measured from merchant-reported order outcomes.
fraud_cluster.outcome_feedback: Outcome impact is measured from merchant-reported delivery, return, and chargeback feedback.

developer.title: Built for developers.
developer.subtitle: One clean REST request. Instant JSON response with transparent risk scores, actionable decisions, and categorized event signals.

roadmap.title: From rules today to intelligence tomorrow.
roadmap.subtitle: We believe in complete architectural honesty. We do not claim nebulous black-box machine learning where proven deterministic rules and entity graphs deliver far greater precision and accountability.
roadmap.phase_1_desc: Transparent heuristic rules, custom threshold controls, and instant rule overrides for immediate merchant defense.
roadmap.phase_2_desc: Cross-dimensional scoring uniting device fingerprinting, ASN network intelligence, and behavioral velocity indicators.
roadmap.phase_3_desc: 3D multi-node correlation joining phone, IP, device, and address to uncover multi-actor syndicates and carding rings.
roadmap.phase_4_desc: Connecting real merchant outcomes (chargebacks, manual approvals, returns) back to evaluated risk scores.
roadmap.phase_5_desc: Adaptive learning models trained exclusively on verified historical merchant outcomes for bespoke merchant tuning.

integrations.subtitle: Receive new orders from WooCommerce or a custom-built store. Each connection belongs to the selected ORDIUM store and reports its latest incoming event.
integrations.select_store: Select an active store from the dashboard header first.
integrations.add_desc: Create a private receiving URL for this connection. ORDIUM stores its signing secret encrypted and only shows it when the connection is created.

integrations.empty_desc: Add a connection above so ORDIUM can start receiving orders from this store.
integrations.never_received: No event has been received from this connection yet.
integrations.payload_desc: Each order must include first and last name, an Algerian phone number, wilaya, commune, delivery address, a positive total, and DZD currency. Convert any provider-specific fields to this format before sending.
integrations.signing_hint: Sign the exact raw JSON body with HMAC-SHA256 using the one-time secret. Put the digest in X-ORDIUM-Signature and send event: order.created.
integrations.woocommerce_step1: In WooCommerce, open Settings, then Advanced, then Webhooks.
integrations.woocommerce_step2: Create a webhook and choose the Order created topic.
integrations.woocommerce_step3: Copy the receiver URL and secret from the connection details shown after creation.
integrations.woocommerce_step4: Paste the URL and secret into WooCommerce, save it, then create a test order.

integrations.secret_warning: Store this secret in your store's webhook settings. Do not share it or place it in browser-side code. ORDIUM will not show it again.

security.subtitle: ORDIUM uses tenant-scoped authorization, credential hashing and encryption, request tracing, and signed webhooks. This page deliberately avoids claiming certifications, retention guarantees, or cryptographic properties that are not implemented and independently verified.
security.p1_desc: API queries are scoped by merchant and by environment (live traffic vs. simulator). Dashboard credentials are kept server-side and reach the browser only through the authenticated control-plane session.
security.title: Security controls that match the current implementation.
security.p3_desc: The current order schema accepts commerce metadata and does not accept PAN or CVV fields. Do not send payment-card credentials to ORDIUM.
security.s3: Webhook HMAC-SHA256 signing with event and delivery identifiers
security.s5: Rate limiting and request IDs for API operations
security.p4_desc: Scoped API keys, request IDs, audit records, idempotency handling, signed webhooks, rate limits, and tenant/environment boundaries are implemented controls. This MVP does not claim compliance certifications.
security.s1: Scoped API-key permissions and merchant isolation
security.p2_desc: API credentials are stored as SHA-256 hashes in the API database. Dashboard session credentials are encrypted before storage in the control-plane database.
security.s2: Live traffic isolated from the simulator, enforced by the API credential

docs.status_409: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource
docs.subtitle: Integrate order-risk evaluation and manual order confirmation through an authenticated REST API with store-scoped credentials, auditable contact attempts, confirmation metrics, and signed webhooks.
docs.status_ok: Request succeeded; 201 when an order is created and evaluated
docs.status_422: Validation failed, or an Idempotency-Key was reused with a different body
docs.general_note: All data is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment and selected store. Rate limits are set by the API configuration. The confirmation workflow records staff actions only; WhatsApp messages and phone calls are never sent automatically.
docs.status_401: Missing, invalid or revoked API key
docs.auth_desc: Send your store API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header on every request. Keys start with ordium_live_ or ordium_test_.
docs.status_403: The key lacks the scope required by this route
docs.webhook_desc: ORDIUM signs every webhook with your endpoint secret and sends the signature in the X-ORDIUM-Signature header as t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>. The signed string is the timestamp, a dot, and the exact request body. Verify it against the raw body before trusting the event.
docs.status_429: Rate limit or usage quota exceeded; retry later

company.title: Order risk intelligence for digital commerce.
company.p3_desc: Scoped credentials, idempotency, request IDs, webhooks, live order processing and an isolated simulator are core product primitives.
company.subtitle: ORDIUM is an engineering project focused on helping commerce platforms evaluate order risk using deterministic signals, identity relationships, and merchant-scoped telemetry.
company.p2_desc: Merchant and environment context is enforced by the API credential and database query scope.
company.security_desc: Security controls and limitations are documented based on the current implementation.
company.dev_desc: Use the developer documentation and dashboard to create scoped integration keys and configure webhooks.
company.p1_desc: Risk decisions expose the persisted signals and rule/profile versions used for evaluation.
company.contact_desc: Contact details will be published here once an official support address and disclosure process are configured.

platform.subtitle: Designed for merchant-scoped checkout risk evaluation. The platform persists risk signals, rule versions, identity relationships, and measured evaluation telemetry.
platform.f1_desc: The dashboard reports measured evaluation time when persisted telemetry is available.
platform.metrics_desc: Track confirmed orders, orders awaiting first contact, work in progress, cancellations and contact attempts. The confirmation rate uses orders with recorded confirmation activity as its denominator; untouched new orders are reported separately.
platform.title: The ORDIUM Risk Engine
platform.f2_desc: Request limits are controlled by the active API environment and merchant configuration.
platform.f3_desc: Persisted assessments expose the risk events, rule version, profile version, and identity context available for review.
platform.manual_desc: Open a pre-filled WhatsApp conversation or start a phone call yourself, then record the result against the order. ORDIUM does not send messages or place calls automatically.
